facts.raw_span: a several-week history of a progressively enlarging swelling on the posterior ulnar aspect of her right forearm
no history of trauma
no systemic symptoms
a firm, non–tender 4 × 5 cm mass was palpated in the subcutaneous tissues of the distal forearm
no overlying skin changes
Neurovascular examination of the hand was normal
Plain radiographs of the forearm showed no fracture
soft-tissue swelling with cortical irregularity of the adjacent ulna
MRI of the right forearm revealed a mass arising from the bone and extending into the soft tissues
the lesion was isointense to muscle on T1-weighted images and heterogeneous hyperintense on T2-weighted images
marked enhancement after gadolinium administration
cortical bone lysis with medullary involvement

concepts.why: The MRI findings of a mass arising from the bone and extending into the soft tissues, with cortical bone lysis and medullary involvement, are highly suggestive of osteosarcoma.
The presence of a mass arising from the bone and extending into the soft tissues, with marked enhancement after gadolinium administration, is consistent with Ewing's Sarcoma.

The cortical irregularity of the adjacent ulna and the presence of a mass arising from the bone are consistent with osteomyelitis, although the lack of systemic symptoms and the specific MRI findings make this diagnosis less likely.

rationales.F01: Progressively enlarging swelling suggests a growing tumor, which is more typical of osteosarcoma or Ewing's sarcoma.
rationales.F09: MRI showing a mass arising from the bone and extending into the soft tissues is highly suggestive of a primary bone tumor like osteosarcoma or Ewing's sarcoma.
rationales.F10: The lesion's appearance on T1 and T2-weighted images, along with marked enhancement after gadolinium administration, is consistent with an aggressive bone tumor.
rationales.F12: Cortical bone lysis with medullary involvement indicates an aggressive process, which is more typical of osteosarcoma or Ewing's sarcoma than osteomyelitis.
